name: Priya Anand
presenting_complaint: Sudden breathlessness and right-sided pleuritic chest pain

conditions: Recent right total knee replacement 10 days ago
medications: Enoxaparin prophylaxis (missed several doses at home)
medical_history.social: Returned from a long-haul flight 3 weeks ago. Non-smoker. Reduced mobility since knee surgery.
medical_history.family: Sister had a DVT during pregnancy.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 47-year-old woman presents with sudden-onset breathlessness and sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain that began 1 hour ago. She is 10 days post right total knee replacement, takes the combined oral contraceptive pill and has a swollen tender right calf. Obs: BP 94/60, HR 124, RR 30, SpO2 89% on room air. She looks anxious and clammy with borderline hypotension.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: SOCRATES of pain: sudden-onset right-sided pleuritic chest pain, worse on inspiration, associated acute breathlessness
VTE risk factors: recent knee arthroplasty 10 days ago, combined oral contraceptive pill, long-haul flight, obesity, reduced mobility, family history of VTE
Symptoms of DVT: unilateral right calf swelling, pain and tenderness
Red-flag/haemodynamic screen: syncope/presyncope, haemoptysis; document borderline hypotension (SBP 94) — pre-shock, does not yet meet the massive/high-risk threshold of SBP <90
Bleeding-risk and anticoagulation history documented (recent surgery, missed enoxaparin doses) before starting anticoagulation
objective: A-to-E assessment, high-flow oxygen, IV access x2 and continuous cardiac + SpO2 monitoring
12-lead ECG (look for sinus tachycardia, right heart strain, S1Q3T3) and portable CXR to exclude alternatives
Calculate a Wells score for PE to establish pretest probability
Examine legs for DVT (unilateral calf swelling/tenderness) and assess for signs of right heart strain (raised JVP, loud P2)
Bloods: FBC, UEC, coags, troponin and BNP for risk stratification; beta-hCG (pregnancy test) before imaging; D-dimer ONLY if low/moderate probability
assessment: High pretest-probability pulmonary embolism (high Wells score) — intermediate-high-risk / pre-shock PE with borderline hypotension (SBP 94, not yet <90) and hypoxia
Stratify as intermediate-high-risk / pre-shock (borderline hypotension) — treat and closely monitor while investigating; escalate to a resuscitation if SBP falls <90
Consider differentials: acute coronary syndrome, aortic dissection, pneumothorax, pneumonia, pericardial tamponade
plan: Resuscitate: high-flow oxygen titrated to SpO2, IV access, cautious IV fluid, continuous monitoring — treat and closely monitor the borderline-hypotensive patient while investigating (FIRST)

Commence therapeutic anticoagulation immediately in high pretest probability — do NOT delay for imaging (e.g. enoxaparin 1 mg/kg subcut BD (12-hourly), or IV unfractionated heparin infusion if the patient becomes unstable/thrombolysis is being considered)
Arrange urgent CTPA once stabilised (V/Q scan if renal impairment, contrast allergy or pregnancy)

If the patient deteriorates to true haemodynamic instability (SBP <90 / obstructive shock): call ED consultant and ICU and consider systemic thrombolysis (e.g. alteplase) after weighing bleeding risk from recent surgery (thrombolysis is relatively contraindicated 10 days post-arthroplasty)
Check no contraindications and quantify bleeding risk (recent knee replacement) before anticoagulation/thrombolysis
Analgesia for pleuritic pain, treat hypoxia, and admit under medical team with ICU/HDU review
Serial obs, repeat ECG/troponin, and document VTE prophylaxis review and reason for missed enoxaparin

critical_errors: Withholding anticoagulation while awaiting CTPA in a patient with high pretest probability of PE — the make-or-break error

Treating a borderline-hypotensive (pre-shock) PE as low-risk/stable and sending the patient off the monitored area to CT unaccompanied instead of resuscitating, monitoring closely and preparing to escalate
Sending a D-dimer in a high pretest-probability patient and using a result to withhold imaging/treatment

Failing to give therapeutic anticoagulation, or failing to escalate to ICU/senior review if the patient deteriorates to true haemodynamic instability (SBP <90); note routine thrombolysis is NOT indicated at SBP 94 and is relatively contraindicated 10 days post-arthroplasty
must_not_miss: Intermediate-high-risk / pre-shock PE with borderline hypotension requiring close monitoring, immediate therapeutic anticoagulation and readiness to escalate (thrombolysis reserved for true instability, SBP <90)
Therapeutic anticoagulation started without delay in high pretest probability (not withheld for the scan)
Aortic dissection and ACS considered/excluded before/alongside anticoagulation
Bleeding risk from recent knee arthroplasty weighed before any thrombolysis
